children: SBI economists expect the RBI to begin a rate hike cycle, citing rising inflationary pressures, higher crude oil prices and global economic uncertainty, with another increase likely in December

The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is expected to begin a rate hike cycle with an increase of at least 25 basis points in its October policy review, according to economists at the State Bank of India (SBI).

SBI’s Economic Research Department (ERD) has advocated a pre-emptive 25-basis-point increase in the benchmark repo rate from the current 5.25 per cent to 5.5 per cent, arguing that the balance of risks has shifted towards tighter monetary policy.
The MPC is scheduled to meet from October 5 to 7, with its policy decision expected on October 7. The proposed increase would be the first repo rate hike since February 2023.

The SBI economists have also called for a further 25-basis-point increase in December, signalling a possible shift towards monetary tightening after a prolonged period of rate cuts and policy stability.
Inflation And Global Risks Strengthen Case For Hike

The SBI economists have cited broadening inflationary pressures, worsening global macroeconomic conditions, evolving liquidity dynamics and a renewed repricing of global risks as key reasons for the proposed rate increase.

Higher crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical tensions, have added to concerns over imported inflation. Oil prices crossing the $100-per-barrel mark have increased the risk of higher input costs and further pressure on domestic prices. SBI Research has warned that crude oil could rise further if geopolitical uncertainties persist.

Inflationary pressures have also become more widespread. Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July, exceeding the RBI's 4 per cent medium-term target for the third consecutive month. Stronger food and energy prices have contributed to the increase.

At the same time, India's economic growth has remained resilient, giving the central bank some room to focus on inflation risks. GDP growth stood at 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter of FY27, reinforcing the case for a possible shift in the monetary policy stance.
SBI Expects Upward Revision In Growth And Inflation Forecasts

Alongside the proposed rate increase, SBI economists expect the RBI to revise its FY27 growth forecast upwards by 30 basis points to 7 per cent from 6.7 per cent. They also anticipate a 20-basis-point increase in the inflation projection to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent.
The projected revisions reflect the changing economic outlook, with stronger-than-anticipated growth coinciding with rising price pressures and external risks.

The anticipated rate hike comes after the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent in its August policy review, marking the fourth consecutive policy meeting without a change. The central bank had reduced the repo rate by a cumulative 125 basis points during 2025.

Expectations of a shift in policy have also gained ground among other economists. A Reuters poll conducted in September found that nearly 60 per cent of economists surveyed expected a 25-basis-point increase in October, while several anticipated another hike by December.

The October policy decision will therefore be closely watched for signals on the RBI's response to inflation, currency pressures and global monetary tightening, as well as the likely pace of any subsequent rate increases.
